patch.value: GH-1134: required collection recovery omits truthful --clear-* intent

GitHub #1134 shows that strict required-field refusals suggest only value-bearing collection flags or progressive mode even though --clear-deps and the other --clear-* flags are the truthful considered-empty answer, steering agents toward fabricated context edges.

Required collection failures map each supported collection to its exact --clear-* considered-empty flag; suggested_flags rank the truthful clear intent before value-bearing or policy-bypass alternatives; examples explain both empty and populated forms without invented identifiers; structured recovery and human diagnostics remain contract-parity; SDK CLI MCP completions and docs expose the same semantics; executable negative controls prove every advertised recovery succeeds without dangling or fabricated data; focused acceptance transcript and exact repository coverage gates pass
pm 2026.8.23 with governance.preset=strict in an empty initialized workspace

Configure strict governance, invoke create with every required field except --dep, inspect suggested_flags and examples, then compare the advertised routes with the successful unadvertised --clear-deps command.
A missing required collection refusal advertises the exact truthful considered-empty flag first and every suggested recovery is executable.
The refusal advertises --dep and progressive mode but omits --clear-deps, so its easiest successful path either invents a relationship or abandons configured policy.
required-field recovery bundles and create option policy
Agents following first-party recovery guidance can permanently pollute the context graph with false edges that appear fully provenance-backed.
